# Issue #294 notes (claude-3, opus)
- Branch clean at start: the earlier devin run's bot/ edits were put back by the path guard; nothing delivered.
- Whole change is under bot/ (forbidden_paths in .harness/config.json; prompt "Never" rule 1). Plan itself says a person must build it.
- Nothing outside bot/ implements /harness commands. Decision: report blocked, no edits.
handoff.reason: the builder needs a person to decide something

294.question: Every line of #294 is under `bot/` (`bot/harness/providers.py`, `__main__.py`, `dashboard.py`, `commands.py`, `events.py`, a new `bot/tests/test_suspend.py`, `bot/README.md`). The bot may not change `bot/`: it is in `forbidden_paths` in `.harness/config.json`, the path guard puts such edits back, and that is why the earlier devin run delivered nothing. Raising the difficulty doesn't change this, because the limit is on the path, not the model tier. Which do you want? (a) Relabel #294 `human` and have a person apply the plan in the issue description. It still applies line for line: `git diff a6a6b63e 08bec482 -- bot/` is empty. (b) Have a person commit a change to `.harness/config.json` that lets the bot edit `bot/` for this item. I don't recommend this, because the `bot selftest` gate would then be judging the bot's own change to itself. (c) Narrow the issue to a part outside `bot/`. I found none, since `/harness` commands are handled only in `bot/harness/`.

# PR #334 conflict revision (merge of main 97a00bd6)

## Status: blocked (pushed nothing)

`pending/v0.2.Y.json` collides with main's Gary micro patch (#324), which also sits at
`pending/v0.2.Y.json`. A fragment's file name must equal its version (`checkFragments`), and a micro
patch's only version is `v0.2.Y`, so two micro fragments cannot both be pending.
- This branch's fragment alone: `patches check` fails ("core-004" unclaimed). Verified.
- Main's fragment alone: this branch's six cards are unclaimed.
- Both merged into one fragment: `patches check` passes, but `patches ship` refuses it later,
  because ship proves each fragment against the catalog of the commit that *added* it (16724d26
  changed only core-004). That would break main's promotion. Rejected.
- Renaming this patch to a bare number (v0.2.18) contradicts the designer's micro title. Rejected
  without a person's say-so.

The fix: wait for `origin/patches/ship-97a00bd6` ("patches ship: v0.2.16b, v0.2.17", which deletes
main's v0.2.Y.json) to merge, then revise again. The fragment then merges cleanly.

## The other conflicts (mechanical; redo them the same way next time)
- BUILD.md:337: main's rarity line (32/40/16/7/5, v0.2.17) + this branch's tag list.
- SPEC.md §5 tags row: this branch's row with "Plague Tokens" -> "Plague Counters" (R740).
- SPEC.md §8 rarity paragraph: main's text with "Solarius-Prime" -> "Solarius Prime".
- SPEC.md R630/R631: this branch's R630 ("Prime, AI and Token") + main's R631 (adds C+ #29).
- catalog.test.ts header and catalog-types.ts doc comment: this branch's text, "Plague Tokens" ->
  "Plague Counters".
handoff.reason: the builder needs a person to decide something

334.question: This branch's patch fragment and main's Gary micro patch (#324) both need the file `packages/cards/patches/pending/v0.2.Y.json`. A fragment's file name has to match its version, and `v0.2.Y` is the only name a micro patch can have, so the two can't both be pending at once. Main's promotion pull request on branch `patches/ship-97a00bd6` ("patches ship: v0.2.16b, v0.2.17") ships Gary and deletes that file. Should I (a) wait until that promotion merges and then revise again, which I recommend? The fragment then merges cleanly and the other conflicts are mechanical. Or (b) rename this patch's fragment to a fixed number such as v0.2.18 now? That goes against the issue's micro `v0.2.Y` title.
